label: KMT2A::MLLT6

sections.text: KMT2A encodes a chromatin regulator that controls developmental and hematopoietic transcription, including HOX genes.

audit_evidence.location: NCBI Gene 4297 RefSeq/Alliance summary, inspected cached esummary record
audit_evidence.scope: Normal partner description only; not primary fusion evidence.

sections.text: MLLT6 encodes MLLT6/AF17, a PHD-finger-containing protein.

audit_evidence.location: Approved HGNC snapshot row HGNC:7138 / MLLT6
audit_evidence.scope: Normal partner description only; not primary fusion evidence.

sections.text: KMT2A::MLLT6 is a recurrent KMT2A fusion in acute leukemia, documented by genomic breakpoint analysis in a large patient cohort.

audit_evidence.location: Results; Table 1; Figure 2; disease distributions at lines 810-825
audit_evidence.scope: Patient-level detection and recurrent partner distribution; no blanket proof of menin/HOXA/MEIS1 mechanism.

sections.text: In adult AML treated with intensive regimens, non-MLLT3 KMT2A rearrangements fall in the adverse ELN 2022 genetic-risk group.

audit_evidence.location: Table 6, 2022 ELN risk classification by genetics at initial diagnosis
audit_evidence.scope: Favorable CBF; intermediate t(9;11); adverse DEK::NUP214, other KMT2A, MECOM and KAT6A::CREBBP categories.

sections.text: Revumenib has a US indication for relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation in adults and children aged at least 1 year.

audit_evidence.location: FDA approval notice, indication paragraph and Efficacy and Safety
audit_evidence.scope: Approved KMT2A-translocation class, not equivalent efficacy for every individual partner.

report_comment.text: KMT2A encodes a chromatin regulator that controls developmental and hematopoietic transcription, including HOX genes. MLLT6 encodes MLLT6/AF17, a PHD-finger-containing protein. KMT2A::MLLT6 is a recurrent KMT2A fusion in acute leukemia, documented by genomic breakpoint analysis in a large patient cohort. In adult AML treated with intensive regimens, non-MLLT3 KMT2A rearrangements fall in the adverse ELN 2022 genetic-risk group. Revumenib has a US indication for relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation in adults and children aged at least 1 year.
